correctness.rationale: Explicit Klein radial bound, primitive and area normalization reconstruct the exact CDF and density; tangent-contact expansion verified by differentiating arccos. Fixed-n cusp mark density converges and integrates to 1; exact survival normalizer plus Scheffe yields total variation. Rescaled many-side joint density converges pointwise to normalized arcsine–exponential; Scheffe yields TV, and compact-angle truncation gives centered-distance weak limit. Independent endpoint-substitution quadrature and large-n numerical tests were rerun successfully.

originality.rationale: The accessible archived 51M20 source and five closely relevant full scientific results were inspected. The closest ideal-polygon results treat nearest-side distance or distances between two random points, not the fixed-incenter distance. The Euclidean polar radial law does not imply the hyperbolic cusp or many-side marks. No matching exact law, marked cusp factorization, or arcsine–exponential limit was identified. Priority remains provisional because broader classical disk-intersection formulas might imply the elementary component.
residual_risks: The exact finite-n CDF may be implicit in older hyperbolic polar/ball-intersection geometry that is not searchable by the terms used.
Marked fixed-n or growing-side probability laws may have unindexed equivalents; published priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The exact distance-to-symmetry-center distribution is a geometrically natural invariant of fixed finite-area regular ideal polygons; the density contact cusp quantifies when expanding metric disks first hit sides. The marked rare-cusp law and growing-side arcsine/exponential factorization describe distinct, motivated geometric regimes, giving probability distributions not determined by polygon area or previously available nearest-side/two-point statistics. Value does not depend on a future downstream theorem.
